title: Understanding the Task
text: When predicting a disease, it's crucial to minimize false negatives. A false negative occurs when the model predicts a person does not have the disease when they actually do. This can lead to missed diagnoses and lack of treatment.

title: Evaluating Thresholds
text: Consider how each threshold affects the number of false negatives. A lower threshold means more people are predicted to have the disease, reducing the chance of missing someone who actually has it.

hintAnswer: Model A minimizes false negatives because it predicts positive for lower probabilities, reducing the chance of missing a true positive.
title: Analyzing Model A
text: Model A uses a threshold of $$T=0.25$$. This means any predicted probability of $$0.25$$ or higher will result in a positive prediction. How does this affect false negatives?
choices: Model A minimizes false negatives because it predicts positive for lower probabilities, reducing the chance of missing a true positive.
Model A increases false negatives because it predicts positive for higher probabilities, increasing the chance of missing a true positive.

title: Comparing Models
text: Compare the thresholds of Models B and C with Model A. Which model is more likely to predict a positive result for a given probability?

hintAnswer: Model A, since we want to minimize false negatives.
title: Choosing the Best Model
text: Given the need to minimize false negatives, which model is best suited for predicting disease presence?
choices: Model A, since we want to minimize false positives.
Model A, since we want to minimize false negatives.
Model B, since it balances precision and recall.
Model C, since we want to minimize false negatives.
Model C, since we want to maximize precision.
